criteria.group: Guideline 1: Epistemic & Data Integrity (Robustness of Training & Context Data)
criteria.title: Provenance & Grounding
criteria.supplied_wording: All ingested knowledge, retrieval-augmented context (RAG), and training inputs must carry verifiable metadata regarding source, recency, and confidence level, preventing agents from treating stale or unverified data as deterministic truth.
criteria.qualification: Local provisional A/AA labels only; retain implementation notes on provenance/uncertainty, accessible role-based transparency, bounded intervention and recovery, tested fallbacks and model-change evaluation. No measured pass/fail, validated conformance or deployed control is asserted.

criteria.group: Guideline 2: Execution & Architectural Compatibility (Robustness of Implementation)
criteria.title: Capability, Intent, State
criteria.supplied_wording: Every tool, API, and sub-agent action must programmatically expose its exact schema (capability), expected outcome (intent), and real-time execution status (state) using open, model-agnostic protocols (such as MCP or OpenAPI) rather than brittle prompt hacks.

criteria.title: Deterministic Guardrails & Graceful Degradation
criteria.supplied_wording: When a tool fails, an API times out, or confidence drops below threshold, the system must fail safely—preserving state, rolling back partial side effects, and falling back to deterministic logic or human escalation without corrupting downstream workflows.
